package_info.package_versions: 2019.4 HF 5 through 2020.2.1 HF 1 (approximate, based on public reporting)
package_info.why_malicious: The SolarWinds Orion software supply chain was compromised, resulting in the distribution of a backdoored update (Sunburst) to thousands of customers. The malicious code enabled remote access and control by attackers, facilitating widespread espionage and data exfiltration.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time (service startup) and during runtime, the code checks if the process is 'solarwinds.businesslayerhost.exe', verifies network connectivity, beacons to the hardcoded C2 domain 'avsvmcloud.com', receives attacker commands, and executes them, enabling remote control and data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code initiates unauthorized outbound network connections to a hardcoded external command-and-control (C2) domain and enables remote command execution, which is not expected in legitimate Orion updates.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Orion updates should not contain logic that beacons to external C2 domains or executes arbitrary remote commands received from the internet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate software may check for updates or send telemetry, but not with obfuscated C2 logic or the ability to execute arbitrary remote commands.
key_indicators: Obfuscated network communication logic within core business DLL

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time (service startup), the code checks if the environment domain is 'solarwinds.com', or if a debugger or virtual machine is detected, and immediately terminates execution to evade detection by security researchers.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The presence of anti-analysis and anti-debugging logic is a hallmark of malware attempting to evade detection and analysis by security tools or researchers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate business logic should not terminate based on environment, domain, or analysis checks, as this disrupts normal operation and serves no business purpose.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some DRM or licensing systems may use environment detection, but not to evade security analysis or terminate core business logic.
key_indicators: Debugger and virtual machine detection with early exit
Obfuscated anti-analysis logic embedded in business logic assembly

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is injected into the SolarWinds Orion build pipeline and distributed via software update.
attack_chain.leads_to: Deployment of backdoored software to customer environments

attack_chain.action: Upon service startup, the malicious DLL performs anti-analysis checks to evade detection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of C2 beaconing logic if not in analysis environment

attack_chain.action: Malicious code beacons to external C2 domain and awaits attacker instructions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote command execution and potential data exfiltration

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections from Orion services to avsvmcloud.com or related C2 domains
Presence of obfuscated or non-standard logic in SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll
Anti-analysis checks (domain, debugger, VM) embedded in business logic assemblies
file_indicators: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll with unexpected hash or file size
Presence of unknown or modified DLLs in the Orion installation directory
network_indicators: Connections to avsvmcloud.com and related C2 infrastructure
Beaconing patterns from Orion servers to external IPs or domains not associated with SolarWinds
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected outbound connections from SolarWinds Orion servers to known C2 domains such as avsvmcloud.com. Perform file integrity checks on SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll to detect unauthorized modifications. Analyze business logic assemblies for anti-analysis or obfuscated code. Correlate findings with threat intelligence on known Sunburst indicators to confirm compromise.
